day_shape: 76 items: IRGC Navy claims two tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, IDF confirms killing Hamas official Khaled Abu Nada in Deir al-Balah, Khamenei issues Basij Week message calling for 'new birth' of the force, CENTCOM reports Syrian seizure of IRGC weapons bound for Lebanon, Iran International flags underground construction near nuclear sites and fifth day of truckers' strike, one UK Parliament written question tabled.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker explosions
threads.summary: The IRGC Navy said two tankers, including a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude, were hit by sea mines and caught fire north of Khasab after deviating from authorised routes. IRGC Navy commander Rear Adm. Azmayee separately claimed the Strait of Hormuz is under full Iranian operational control.

threads.label: IDF strike on Hamas official in Deir al-Balah
threads.summary: Israeli military correspondents and the Jerusalem Post reported the IDF and Shin Bet killed Khaled Abu Nada, head of Hamas's economy and education portfolios, along with his wife in an overnight strike in Deir al-Balah. Netanyahu and Katz confirmed the killing as part of a series of targeted strikes against Hamas government members.

threads.label: Khamenei Basij Week message cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office released a message for Basij Week declaring the organisation must undergo a 'new birth' and promoting the slogan 'every Iranian, a Basiji'. IRGC commander Vahidi, judiciary chief Ejei and the Jerusalem Post (citing Mojtaba Khamenei) echoed calls to expand the paramilitary force.

threads.label: Iran nuclear and missile developments
threads.summary: Iran International, citing a Washington-based institute, reported rapid construction of a fortified underground complex at Behjatabad between two nuclear sites, with Vantor Technologies satellite imagery cited by the Jerusalem Post. The Jerusalem Post separately reported Iran is developing new ballistic missile variants, while the IRGC spokesman claimed missile stocks exceed US levels.

threads.label: Iran proxy weapons seizures and plots abroad
threads.summary: CENTCOM said Syrian forces seized IRGC weapons bound for Lebanon, Iran International reported German arrests of two Iraqi nationals over a pro-Iranian synagogue plot in Cologne, and Sky News flagged suspected Iran-linked drone threats prompting RAF to shelter aircraft. Iran International also reported Kataib Hezbollah is repositioning in western Iraq ahead of possible renewed US-Iran conflict.

threads.label: Iran economy, blockade and labour unrest
threads.summary: Iran International reported a fifth day of truckers' strikes spreading to 18 cities, and economists warning alternative routes cannot offset US naval blockade losses, while Tehran dismissed the blockade and threatened broader confrontation. Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran will procure needed goods through 'various methods' and keep its conditions for mediators unchanged.

threads.label: Yemen–Saudi strikes and regional friction
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press reported Yemeni forces struck Jazan refinery and Riyadh in response to Saudi airstrikes on Hodeidah and Sahar, and posted footage of smoke rising from Ras Tanura. Separately, Israel's UN ambassador Danon told the Jerusalem Post that Israel opposes a French initiative to deploy troops in southern Lebanon.

events.title: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz confirm the IDF struck and killed a senior Hamas government official in the central Gaza Strip overnight. Khaled Abu Nada was responsible for Hamas's economy and education portfolio, the Israeli leaders say. Netanyahu and Katz say the killing of Abu Nada is "part of a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and senior officials of the organization." "Around 80 Hamas terrorists have been killed over the past month, and our forces will continue to thwart and exact retribution against every terrorist in the terror organization," the joint statement adds.
